title: Shard-aware Redis Streams consumer refactor: prefetch, holdoff, and isolated retry budgets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:

Our Redis Streams consumer has accumulated multiple ad-hoc heuristics for prefetching, retry shaping, and backpressure that were added in fast iterations. This has produced brittle behavior under mixed workloads: small low-latency requests are delayed by large-batch tenants, and one noisy message type can exhaust global retry capacity causing head-of-line blocking across shards.

Problem statement:
- Global inflight counters and single retry budget lead to cross-tenant interference and uneven latency tails.
- Prefetch heuristics do not account for shard/consumer-group contention, causing hotspots and amplified rebalances.
- Existing backpressure mechanism is an all-or-nothing shedder; it either accepts or rejects whole fetch cycles which leads to latency cliffs.
- Redis client dependency is behind upstream and lacks a stable stream-consumer backoff helper.

Goals:
1) Introduce per-shard (consumer-group) token buckets to limit inflight per-shard and avoid global interference.
2) Replace global prefetch with shard-aware adaptive prefetch driven by observed processing time percentiles and queue length.
3) Implement graceful holdoff (soft backpressure) that reduces fetch window instead of hard rejections when under pressure.
4) Add isolated retry budgets keyed by message-type + shard so noisy types cannot starve others.
5) Upgrade redis client library to upstream v8.x for improved Streams support and observable hooks.
6) Keep migration safe with a feature flag and gradual rollout, with ability to revert quickly.

Proposed design summary:
- Per-shard metadata tracked in memory: (inflight_tokens, recent_latency_histogram, fetch_window). Token bucket replenishment will be jittered and proportional to consumer capacity.
- Adaptive prefetch: fetch_window = base_window * f(latency_p95, queue_depth); when latency_p95 increases, shrink window; when queue empty, increase slowly.
- Soft holdoff: when token exhaustion occurs, instead of rejecting XREADGROUP calls, reduce fetch_window and sleep with exponentially backed-off jitter to allow KV cache to drain.
- Retry budgets: maintain a small per-type budget (configurable) and a global safety cap. When a type exhausts its budget, it falls back to dead-lettering after a higher-delay backoff.
- Metrics: gauge per-shard inflight, fetch_window, budget_remaining[type], shed_events, holdoff_seconds; events traced to request id for replay.
- Dependency upgrade: move to go-redis v8.x (or equivalent client in lang) to leverage stream consumer helpers and connection pooling fixes. Run compatibility tests against existing Redis 6/7 infra.

Rollout strategy:
1) Feature-flag gated implementation behind "shard_prefetch_refactor".
2) Canary on a low-traffic tenant for 24h with sampling and extra metrics.
3) Expand to 10% of tenants with continuous monitoring of tail latency and error rate.
4) Full rollout only after 72h stable canary and no regression in token cost metrics.
5) Fast rollback plan: flip flag off, drain new metadata, and fall back to current heuristics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for token-bucket semantics and adaptive prefetch cover corner cases (consumer restart, rapid spikes, manual rebalances).
- No >5% increase in mean CPU on consumer hosts at canary at 10% traffic; tail latency (p99) improves or stays equal for 80% of tenants.
- No cross-shard starvation observed in synthetic load tests where one message-type is 100x QPS of others.
- Dependency upgrade passes compatibility matrix for Redis versions used in production.
- Feature flag supports immediate rollback with no message loss or duplication beyond existing guarantees.

Implementation tasks (high-level):
- [ ] Prototype in branch: redis/shard-prefetch-refactor.
- [ ] Implement per-shard token bucket and adaptive prefetch logic.
- [ ] Implement soft holdoff + jitter scheduler.
- [ ] Add per-type retry budget keyed by message type tag.
- [ ] Add extensive metrics + traces.
- [ ] Upgrade redis client to v8.x and run compatibility tests.
- [ ] Load test harness: create mixed workload scripts and run perf baseline + post-change.
- [ ] Docs: update consumer-runbook and console observability mappings.
- [ ] Create feature flag and rollout playbook in ops-runbook.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Incorrect token bucket parameters could throttle healthy shards. Mitigation: conservative defaults, gradual increase, AB tests per-tenant.
- Risk: Client upgrade exposes connection pooling regressions. Mitigation: run greenbox compatibility tests and enable new pool size config.
- Risk: Increased memory for per-shard metadata. Mitigation: bounded retention (LRU evict inactive shards after 1h).

Monitoring & dashboards to add:
- per-shard inflight gauge heatmap
- fetch_window over time per consumer-group
- retry budget exhaustion rate by type
- holdoff events and cumulative holdoff seconds
- consumer host CPU and GC change relative to baseline

Notes on backwards compatibility:
- Message semantics (at-least-once) unchanged. We will not change ACK semantics in this work; only how many messages are fetched and how retries are tracked.

Deliverables:
- PR implementing refactor with tests
- Load test report (before/after) with tail-latency and throughput graphs
- Updated runbook + rollout playbook
- Dashboard snapshots for canary and post-rollout
comments: 2025-02-13 - Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting done with infra and runtime teams. Agreed to target conservative defaults and a feature flag. Rafael to lead implementation. Action: bench current baseline (latency by shard) by 2025-02-20.

2025-02-20 - Rafael Ortega: Baseline bench completed. Observed that top-3 shards account for 62% of inflight and cause median p95 spike from 80ms to 420ms under mixed load. Added bench results to the linked Google Drive doc: https://drive.redwood.example/redis-prefetch-bench (internal).

2025-02-25 - Rafael Ortega: Spike-protected token-bucket prototype landed in branch redis/shard-prefetch-refactor. Initial local tests look good. Created PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1296 (WIP).
2025-02-27 - SRE (Priya Nair): Reviewed rollout playbook. Requested explicit alerting thresholds for holdoff_SECONDS and budget_exhaustion_rate. Added to monitoring checklist.

2025-03-01 - Rafael Ortega: Upgraded go-redis client to v8 in branch; ran compatibility matrix against Redis 6.2 and 7.0 instances. Found a pooling bug on 6.2 under connection churn; adding config gate to limit pool size until we can patch client. Opened issue: GH#1302.

2025-03-03 - Rafael Ortega: Canary started for tenant: internal-canary-01 (low traffic). Telemetry shows per-shard inflight dropping 18% and p99 latency improving by ~12% for the canary tenant after 6 hours. Continuing canary to 24h, monitoring for retry budget exhaustion.
notes: This ticket focuses purely on Redis Streams consumer refactor path. Kafka consumers have a parallel refactor story; coordinate semantics but separate PRs. Keep the default behavior unchanged until the flag is enabled.
acceptance_checklist: Unit tests for token bucket and fetch window logic
